national.line: Kristen Bell told Jimmy Fallon that while she was away filming, husband Dax Shepard bought half a dozen sugary cereals as the week's groceries, and their oldest daughter texted her photos of Dad in the cereal cupboard at 10 p.m. Every house needs an inside source.
Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce passed Tony Gonzalez for an NFL tight end receiving record, even in a Kansas City loss. Silver linings come in red and gold.
A Queens man named Joshua Service cleaned up an illegal dumping site he passed on his train commute in New York City, all on his own. With that last name, what else could he do?

Five cheetah cubs born in early October to a mom named Zura at the Smithsonian's Conservation Institute in Virginia can be watched day and night on a live webcam. Office productivity just dropped five notches.

A dad's list of 'complaints' about his toddler's pretend restaurant is charming the internet, including: 'It's a very clean establishment, but whewww let me tell you about this owner.' One-star manager, five-star cuteness.
A toddler drumming and singing 'Pocketful of Sunshine' with stunning precision has people online calling him a musical prodigy. Meanwhile, we still can't clap on beat.
Halloween spending has climbed to a record 13.5 billion dollars. That's a whole lot of fun-size candy bars.

pride.line: Dean Long, Lebanon High School graduate, was inducted into the Emporia State University baseball Hall of Fame in October. Not bad for a kid from Lebanon.
pride.label: Hall of Fame

pride.line: Lebanon R-3 Schools earned a national Meritorious Budget Award in October. Somebody in that office can really balance a checkbook.
pride.label: National Award

pride.line: Lebanon tennis players Lilly Bradbury, Ava Johnson and Carli Alford earned All District honors in October, Bradbury placing fourth in singles and Johnson and Alford fourth in doubles. Love means nothing in tennis, but this means plenty.
pride.label: All District

pride.line: Brittany Stamm is the new head girls basketball coach at Lebanon High School, named in October. Welcome to the Yellowjacket hive.
pride.label: New Coach

pride.line: Kalem Copling is the new head boys basketball coach at Lebanon High School, named in October. The whistle is officially his.
pride.label: New Coach

pride.line: Lebanon Schools opened the new Robert W. Plaster Center for Student Success in October. A brand-new building with that new-building smell.
pride.label: Grand Opening

pride.line: Marshfield Chevrolet is celebrating 100 years in business in Marshfield this October. A century of handshakes and test drives.
pride.label: 100 Years

pride.line: Bolivar School District posted its best state test scores since Missouri's tests began in 1998, with math proficiency at 56.3 percent, 12.5 points above the state average. Somebody tell the calculators to take a bow.
pride.label: Record Scores

pride.line: Waynesville Career Center culinary students Molly McDermitt, Cycila Keeney and Samantha Etheridge made the finals of the World Food Championships in Indianapolis on Oct. 18 with a dish called Bacon Lover's Christmas. That name alone deserves a trophy.
pride.label: World Food Champs

pride.line: Kyleen Oxendine, a teacher at East Elementary in Waynesville, won the first-quarter Project Teach Award on Oct. 19 for her take-home reading success kits. Homework the kids might actually enjoy.
pride.label: Teacher Award

pride.line: The Waynesville Sixth Grade Center won the traveling Tiger Spirit Trophy again for its first-place finish in the 2026 homecoming parade, announced Oct. 20. Sixth graders, undefeated in spirit.
pride.label: Spirit Trophy

pride.line: Domino's of Waynesville received the Waynesville R-6 Community Recognition Plaque on Oct. 19 for its support of local students. A plaque, delivered in under thirty minutes.
pride.label: Community Award

pride.line: Keith Klostermann, a 30-year educator, is the new city administrator for Osage Beach, appointed in October. From the classroom to City Hall.
pride.label: New Leader

pride.line: The Marshfield High School marching band took fourth place at the Ozark Mountain Marching Festival in Reeds Spring in October. Every step counted.
pride.label: Band Honors

pride.line: Lathan Martin and Boone Shockley of Grand Missouri Bank in Bolivar graduated from the Oklahoma Bankers Association Consumer Lending School in October, two of 64 graduates. Loan officers with diplomas to back it up.
pride.label: Graduates

pride.line: Johnny Carriger of Crocker soccer is KY3's Athlete of the Week after scoring a hat trick in the district championship game while battling illness and injury. Three goals, zero excuses.
pride.label: Athlete of the Week

pride.line: The Macks Creek girls cross country team won the varsity title at the Dixon Invitational in October, and the boys finished second. Fast feet run in that school.
pride.label: Team Title

local.line: The City of Lebanon has a second new logo proposal in the works in October, with a new slogan: 'Build your journey here.' Third time's the charm, if needed.
Lebanon's street, electric, water and wastewater crews trained with two neighboring cities on Oct. 21 for trench and confined-space rescues. Safety drills are what keep the real day boring.
A 21,000-square-foot colonial estate on more than seven acres in Lebanon goes up for online auction in early November, with bidding starting at $995,000. That's a lot of rooms to vacuum.

The Joel E. Barber C-5 school district is considering building a high school onto its existing building, Superintendent Dr. Rachelle Jennings said in October. Buckskins might get to stay home through graduation.
A retro Route 66 diner in St. Robert is being called the Missouri road-trip stop for chicken-fried steak and malts. Gravy is the real destination.
Two new Missouri State Highway Patrol troopers have been assigned to Camden and Miller counties in October. Welcome to the Lake, gentlemen.
A Lake of the Ozarks resort owner plans to buy and renovate the foreclosed Regalia Hotel in Lake Ozark, which has sat quiet this year. Lights back on at the Lake.
Golf at Lake of the Ozarks turns 95 this year, alongside Bagnell Dam's 95th anniversary and Lake Ozark's 60th as a city. That's a lot of birthday candles on one lake.
Webster County's Baby Bridge program officially launched in October after a two-month pilot, helping families with babies and toddlers. New parents need all the backup they can get.
Seymour keeps growing, with an estimated population of 2,247, according to the U.S. Census Bureau. Somebody count the new mailboxes.
A Seymour man bagged a black bear, one of seven harvested in Missouri's Zone 1 by Monday of the fall season's opening weekend. Now that's a story for deer camp.

music.line: Bo Bryan, Luke Bryan's son and a three-star quarterback in the 2027 class, committed to the University of Georgia. Dad's tailgate plans are officially set.
Morgan Wallen scored his 24th number one at country radio with 'Been By Now,' topping the Mediabase chart this week. Number one is basically his default setting.
Zach Bryan's 'Young Manhood and Other Donatable Organs' debuted at number one on Billboard's country albums chart and number two across all genres. Big numbers for something called an EP.
Miranda Lambert will headline the Dallas Cowboys Thanksgiving halftime show for The Salvation Army's Red Kettle Kickoff. Pass the pie and the remote.
Brooks and Dunn, the reigning CMA Vocal Duo of the Year, are working on new music. Boot-scootin' fans, start stretching.
Zach Top brought out Lukas Nelson in Arkansas for a cover of Willie Nelson's 'Last Thing I Needed First Thing This Morning.' Arkansas got a night worth bragging about.
'Idol' winner Hannah Harper sang Dolly Parton's '9 to 5' at Dollywood, in an outfit that paid tribute to another Dolly song. Working nine to five never looked so good.
Florida Georgia Line is expanding its comeback with 'Anything Goes Again: The Festival Tour' in 2027. The cruise is back on the road.
Cody Johnson says Nashville wanted to change him before he found success. Good thing he kept the hat.
Boyz II Men are releasing their first country album. Those harmonies are getting a twang.
Amy Grant and Vince Gill are bringing back 'Christmas at the Ryman' in 2026. Nashville's coziest tradition returns.
Billy Strings won Entertainer of the Year at the IBMA Bluegrass Awards in Chattanooga, Tennessee, his fifth time taking that prize. Five wins, a whole banjo's worth.

weird.line: The Laclede County Record's new reporter, Jadzia Jaynes, says her name and her brothers' names all come from Star Trek: Deep Space Nine, and she owns a sassy, geriatric rabbit named Penny. Live long and report.
A 60-year-old Rhode Island grower's 3,156-pound pumpkin became the first ever over 3,000 pounds, breaking a world record set just one week earlier. That's a lot of pie.

Minnesota grower Travis Gienger won the World Championship Pumpkin Weigh-Off in Half Moon Bay, California, for a fifth time with a 2,389-pound giant, taking home $21,501. Cinderella would need a bigger garage.
A Pennsylvania angler reeled in a record-breaking 36-pound channel catfish. That's not a fish story, that's a fish novel.
Biologists netted an endangered Atlantic sturgeon of more than 200 pounds in a narrow Maryland creek, the largest female ever recorded there. Bigger than most of the biologists.
A basketball team says it broke a world record for the most people in cow costumes. Udderly ridiculous, and we love it.
Seven women who pick a group Halloween theme every year dressed as Mike Myers' movie roles for 2026. Yeah, baby, that's commitment.
Wyoming fossil hunters call them 'squid butts,' and two unusually chunky ones turned out to be a new 160-million-year-old squid relative called a belemnite. Science has the best nicknames.
A large grizzly bear was spotted alone on a snow-covered Alaskan volcano at 7,200 feet. Even bears need some me-time.
Strangers on a California highway joined together to catch a man hanging from a truck, and the rescue video went viral. Heroes don't always wear capes, sometimes they wear seatbelts.
A kitten was rescued from a busy freeway, proving not all cat rescues happen in trees. Nine lives, minus one close call.
A woman says her cat came back home to her a week after her breakup, after allegedly peeing in her ex's new girlfriend's shoes, and the internet says he deserves salmon. Loyalty, cat style.
A Florida woman walked out of Chipotle to find her Tesla being towed, and the company charged $185 to get it back, after she says they completely ruined it. Most expensive burrito bowl ever.
A man in Bosnia rescued an abandoned bear cub named Masa, and now the two are inseparable, with Masa wrapping her paws around him for hugs. Best friend, extra fuzzy.
One hundred ten humanoid robots set a Guinness World Record in China for synchronized dancing. Still better than the office Christmas party.
A drone show in Mysuru, India, set a Guinness World Record with 3,473 drones lighting up the sky. Somebody had a very big remote.
A pair of 16-kilogram gold earrings in Dubai set two Guinness World Records and took 5,840 hours to make. Earlobes everywhere are nervous.
The founder of Chinese motorcycle company ZXMOTO set a Guinness record for the longest motorcycle ride on open water. Don't try that on Truman Lake.
A mysterious 40-meter cone of about a million tons of limestone rising from the Siberian forest has puzzled scientists for 70 years. Mother Nature loves a good mystery.
A massive pumpkin disqualified from a growing competition got a second life as a treat for polar bears. Best consolation prize ever.

humor.line: It marks the day in 1785 when the first Spanish donkeys arrived in Boston as a gift from Spain's King Charles III, and George Washington bred America's first mules from them. Founding father and founding mule breeder.
It traces back to a 1769 diary entry about writer Samuel Johnson hearing of a new machine that drove without horses, powered by turning a handle. The first car had arm-day built in.

A Dallas public relations man named Jeffrey Yarbrough got turned down by the state agriculture department and the Texas Beef Council before a state representative helped make the day official. Persistence, deep-fried.
The word pumpkin comes from the Greek word 'pepon,' which means large melon. So a jack-o'-lantern is technically a carved melon.
Many modern mincemeat recipes don't contain any meat at all. Truth in advertising took the day off.
National Day Calendar created it in 2017 to honor Tennessee as the 16th state to join the Union. Sixteenth in line, first in country music.
Every wheel of this Italian cheese ages at least 12 months, and some age as long as 40 months. Some cheese is older than your toddler.
Scotch-Irish immigrants brought potatoes to New Hampshire in 1719, and today they're grown in all 50 states. Fries for everybody.
The Navy League started it in 1922 and picked the date because it's Theodore Roosevelt's birthday. Happy birthday, Teddy, here's a Navy.
It's the one day to let the office grump complain all they want instead of trying to cheer them up. Today, the grump gets a pass.
The word chocolate traces back to the Aztec word 'xocolatl,' which means bitter water. Thank goodness somebody added sugar.
The Statue of Liberty arrived in New York City in 1885 packed in 214 crates and had to be put back together on what's now Liberty Island. Some assembly required, French edition.
Plush fabric has to stand at least an eighth of an inch thick to count as plush. Your kid's teddy bear passed inspection.
It honors the first public showing of projected moving images, Emile Reynaud's Theatre Optique, in 1892. Cartoons have been keeping kids up ever since.
Its popularity may trace back to Euell Gibbons, whose 1962 book was called 'Stalking the Wild Asparagus.' Watch out, those spears are sneaky.
Colleen Paige, who also created National Dog Day, started it, and about 90 million house cats live in the United States. She plays fair, unlike the cat.
It marks 1969, when the first electronic message went from one computer to another on ARPANET, which connected just four terminals, including UCLA and Stanford. Four computers, zero cat videos.
Oats get heated as groats, which gives them their nutty flavor, and steel-cut oats are sliced with actual steel blades. Breakfast, now with blades.
The first doughnuts in America were little 'nuts' of dough brought to New England by the Pilgrims, who learned to make them in Holland. Pilgrims: thankful and glazed.
Legend says breadsticks were invented in Turin, Italy, in the seventeenth century by a court baker named Antonio Brunero. Unlimited ever since.
Candy corn is made from sugar, corn syrup and confectioner's wax. Yes, wax. Happy Halloween.
It lands less than a week after National Pumpkin Day, so those leftover pumpkins finally have a purpose. Recycling never tasted so good.
Scientists think lemurs floated to Madagascar on rafts of vegetation and evolved there over millions of years. World's longest float trip.
Rebecca Morgan started handing out books instead of candy to trick-or-treaters at her San Jose, California, home in 1995. Bold move on the cavity front.
Candy maker William W. Kolb created an early candy apple in Newark, New Jersey, in 1908 while experimenting with red cinnamon candy. Best science experiment in candy history.
Some believe knock-knock jokes grew out of call-and-answer routines that medieval castle guards used to identify visitors after dark. Orange you glad they kept it?
It's an official excuse for grown-ups to eat some of the trick-or-treat candy before the kids start knocking. Call it quality control.
It started in Philadelphia in 1950 with kids collecting coins in decorated milk cartons, and that first year raised 17 dollars. Seventeen bucks and a whole lot of heart.
The Halloween and Costume Association created it in 2019 after petitioning to move Halloween to the last Saturday in October. This year, Halloween finally agreed.
People in Ireland and Britain carved turnips long before pumpkins took over the job. Pumpkins were a big upgrade.
Author Nancy Christie came up with it so people would spend the extra hour from the time change relaxing instead of working. Nap responsibly.
The name calzone translates to trousers or pant legs. Pizza, now wearing pants.
Spice company McCormick created it in 2019 to kick off what it calls cinnamon season. Convenient timing for a spice company.
Nellie Verne Burt McPherson dreamed it up in 1928 to thank her favorite author, Irving Bacheller. The ultimate fan letter.
In 1884, 25 nations met in Washington, D.C., and picked Greenwich, England, as zero longitude, with Haiti voting no and Brazil and France sitting it out. Even maps need a starting line.
